name: Palladian Gravemind Relay Hub
description:
The Gravemind Relay Hub is a distributed mesh-coordination device roughly the size of a hardcover book, constructed from Palladian Construction's proprietary stress-ceramic housing. It operates by seeding a local area with micro-relay dust — particles thin enough to drift through ventilation systems and settle on surfaces — which collectively form a self-organizing signal lattice. The hub itself acts as the root node, stitching the dust-relays into a coherent network that can support up to forty-eight simultaneous encrypted voice and data channels across a radius of roughly six city blocks.

What distinguishes the Gravemind from conventional mesh nodes is its passive topology — the dust-relays require no active power draw, harvesting ambient EM bleed from nearby infrastructure to sustain themselves. This makes the network nearly undetectable by standard sweep equipment, as there is no central transmitter to locate. Traffic is fragmented and distributed across hundreds of micro-nodes before being reconstructed at the receiving end, a process Palladian markets as 'architectural encryption.'

The hub is favored by fixers and mid-tier syndicate operations that need persistent comms infrastructure in contested urban zones without the risk of a single point of compromise. Construction crews operating in corporate exclusion zones use them to maintain coordination when standard channels are jammed or monitored. Law enforcement occasionally finds decommissioned units months after an operation has concluded, the dust long settled into the walls.

specifications.detection_resistance: High — no central EM signature above ambient noise floor
specifications.power_source: Micro-cell battery, 18-hour active operation; passive network persists independently

tactical_use: Operators seed the relay dust through ventilation intake, open windows, or by foot traffic prior to an operation. Once dispersed, the hub is activated from a concealed position to initialize the lattice. Team members connect via standard encrypted handsets without needing line-of-sight or proximity to each other. The hub can be physically removed or destroyed after seeding — the dust network will persist autonomously for days, making post-op signal sweeps ineffective. Used extensively for multi-team operations requiring persistent comms in environments where active transmitters would draw attention.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's underground economy, owning a Gravemind Hub signals a certain level of operational sophistication — it's not the tool of a street runner but of someone who plans three days ahead. Palladian Construction's branding as an infrastructure company lends the device an almost bureaucratic legitimacy; the hardware looks like a contractor's survey unit at a glance. Among fixers, gifting a Gravemind Hub to a trusted associate is considered a significant gesture of partnership, implying you're building something together that outlasts a single job.
known_users: Underground labor organizers in corporate exclusion zones
GLMZ PD tactical units (confiscated and repurposed)
story_hooks: A Gravemind Hub seeded during a job three months ago is still active — and someone is using its ghost network to route communications the original operators never authorized.
The players discover relay dust in their safehouse walls, suggesting the location has been used as an unwitting relay node for an unknown operation.

Palladian Construction is quietly recalling a specific batch of Gravemind Hubs, claiming a firmware defect — but the real reason may be that a back-channel kill-switch was discovered by an independent researcher.
A dying fixer's last message directs the players to a Gravemind Hub she seeded before her final job — the dust network is the only record of what she found.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately austere rectangular slab resembling a hardcover book or thick architectural digest. The top surface is slightly convex, suggesting the curvature of contained pressure. Two recessed grip channels run along the long edges. The front face presents a minimalist control interface with no visible seams where panels meet housing.
physical_description.dimensions: 22cm × 14cm × 6cm (hardcover book-sized, fits under one arm or into a large jacket pocket when carrying strap is removed)
physical_description.weight_description: 1.1kg — handheld, light enough for prolonged carry on a shoulder strap or hip-mounted bracket, but substantial enough to feel engineered
physical_description.primary_material: Palladian proprietary stress-ceramic composite; industrial-grade, designed to survive rough field conditions and temperature cycling
physical_description.finish: Matte ceramicized surface with micro-texturing to improve grip; shows minor scuff marks and dust accumulation in normal use, mimicking field-deployed equipment
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary body with darker charcoal stress-relief striping along seams and edges. Accent elements in pale industrial blue (power/status indicators). Manufacturer nameplate in brushed aluminum inlay.
physical_description.interface_elements: Front panel: small circular dimple-button (power toggle), three status LED indicators (green/amber/red for network integrity, dust capacity, and power), and a semi-flush data port (encrypted micro-connector). Right edge: two analog dials (one for relay-dust dispersal rate, one for channel fragmentation depth). Top surface: covered canister lock with fine machined ridges for manual reload.
distinctive_features: Pressure-relief vents disguised as decorative striping along the bottom edge, allowing passive EM harvesting
Top-mounted rotating canister lock (appears similar to a camera lens cap) with graduation markers for dust-dispersal tracking
Faint ghosting of internal circuitry visible through translucent corner sections of the ceramic housing
Weighted base with adhesive-backed rubber pads, allowing temporary mounting to walls or underside of furniture
Asymmetric cooling fins on the underside, barely visible without inspection
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION logo (stylized Φ in a geometric frame) stamped into aluminum nameplate on front. Regulatory compliance stamps in tiny text on rear: GLMZ Tier 2+ certification, power consumption rating, and a faded serial number. Small warning symbol indicating micro-relay dust handling precautions.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deployed units show wear: dust accumulation in vent striping, minor scuff marks on corners and grip channels, occasional corrosion bloom around the data port. The status LEDs are perpetually illuminated when active, cycling between green and amber. The canister lock often shows tool marks from field reloads.
